absent: Locking or concurrency rules for node assignment, configuration register programming and global base publication.
Full behaviour of K5 initialization before the multiprocessor certification tail shown here.
Remaining erratum 1386 handling and later Zen family initialization sequences beyond the truncated portion.
Numeric values of control registers, capability bits and configuration fields referenced only by symbolic names.
Implementation of firmware table probing, platform correction hooks and suspend resume preservation for hidden capabilities.
Structure layouts for processor description, match entries and PCI probe tables beyond fields referenced here.
Exact bus range encoding and address mask constants used in configuration register programming.

findings.text: Provides a cross file routine that examines processor capability flags for cache monitoring support and records the maximum resource identifier, occupancy scaling factor and bandwidth counter width for later use.
Exposes a predicate that checks a caller supplied match table against the running processor and validates that the boot processor microcode level satisfies the table required minimum.

Exposes a routine that reconciles application processor memory mapped PCI configuration settings with the boot processor setting and programs the control register to enable a full bus segment when appropriate.
Exposes a boot time hook that consults firmware identification data to determine whether memory mapped PCI configuration handling should be considered.

Acts as the boot processor initialization entry for AMD processors, ordering counter validation, address alignment setup, delay mechanism selection, speculative control fallback, cache accounting detection, generation classification and final security mitigations.

Acts as the early per processor initialization entry that establishes baseline capabilities and microcode level, power related features, calling convention behaviour, identifier width handling and encryption state before family specific work.
Provides separate family specific initialization entries for the K8, GH, LN, JG and BD groups, each applying model dependent workarounds and capability adjustments relevant to that group.

Node lookup for a given APIC identifier scans downward from that identifier and then upward, returning the first mapping that is both assigned and online, and falls back to the first online node when no neighbour qualifies.

NUMA placement for the current processor starts from the operating system assignment or last level cache identifier, applies a platform correction hook when present, and when offline first tries the HyperTransport derived mapping indexed by the initial APIC identifier before neighbour search, finally binding the processor to the selected node.

Vendor tracking is set to AMD on the boot processor. Host secure nested paging is retained only when the feature is reported, execution is not virtualized, a recognized recent generation or architectural read capability exists and firmware table probing succeeds; otherwise the feature and platform attribute are withdrawn.

Side channel handling skips virtualized guests. On bare metal with recent Zen generations a clearing capability is forced only when current microcode meets per model minima recorded in a dedicated table, with a debug log otherwise; on other models two immunity indicators are forced unconditionally.

Minimum revision evaluation succeeds only when a table entry matches the running processor and the boot processor revision is at least the entry required value; missing match or older revision yields failure.

Family 0x17 models 0x00 to 0x2f and 0x50 to 0x5f select Zen1 while models 0x30 to 0x4f and 0x60 to 0x7f and 0x90 to 0x91 and 0xa0 to 0xaf select Zen2. Family 0x19 models 0x00 to 0x0f and 0x20 to 0x5f select Zen3 while models 0x10 to 0x1f and 0x60 to 0xaf select Zen4. Family 0x1a models 0x00 to 0x2f and 0x40 to 0x4f and 0x60 to 0x7f and 0xd0 to 0xd7 select Zen5 while models 0x50 to 0x5f and 0x80 to 0xaf and 0xc0 to 0xcf and 0xd8 to 0xef select Zen6.

On families above 0x10 and on recent models of 0x10 with constant counter support, a hardware configuration register is read and a firmware defect is reported when a specific bit indicates the counter does not use the base frequency.

On family 0x15, cache associativity information is used to compute an alignment mask for virtual addresses, both narrow and wide alignment modes are enabled, and a per boot random offset constrained by the mask is installed.

On families 0x15 to 0x17 without either hardware speculative control, a family specific configuration bit is chosen, the current configuration value is cached through a fault tolerant read, and on success two mitigation capabilities are forced with the bit recorded as a mask; a fault leaves mitigations disabled.

When neither occupancy nor bandwidth monitoring is indicated, monitoring parameters are marked absent. Otherwise the maximum identifier is taken from a standard leaf, and when any occupancy or bandwidth capability exists the identifier limit, scale and width are refined from a subleaf, with vendor specific defaults applied for two vendors when width reads as zero.

Memory encryption handling first flags possible cache incoherence for later kexec when an extended leaf advertises encryption support. When either main capability is present, firmware enablement is checked, physical address width is reduced by the reported encryption bit count, and capabilities for encrypted memory and its extensions are withdrawn when firmware has not enabled them, when running in reduced word size, when no encryption mask exists, or when a configuration lock is clear.

Processors reporting encryption support are marked as having incoherent cache state so that kexec transitions between encrypted and unencrypted modes flush stale entries and avoid aliasing of identical physical addresses with different encryption attributes.

Early setup records a baseline capability for families at or above 0x0f, captures microcode level via a fault tolerant read, derives counter and power monitoring features from power leaf bits, selects system call or memory type behaviour by word size and model, widens APIC identifier handling by family or PCI configuration when the controller exists, unconditionally enables a virtualization call convention, applies a family 0x16 configuration fix, and conditionally enables branch flushing controls outside virtualization based on family and a fault tolerant write test.

K8 setup enables an optimized string capability for defined signature intervals, withdraws a load store capability on early models outside virtualization while clearing a related control bit through safe access, supplies Hammer as default model name when empty, disables a TLB filter under multiprocessor builds, and records fence and idle defects with the latter gated by model and stepping thresholds.

GH setup considers memory mapped configuration on the boot processor, suppresses a GART error report, preserves write combining by clearing a configuration bit with a virtualization safe accessor, and records translation defects with an idle erratum gated by model and stepping.

Configuration handling respects a global probe permission. When enablement is already indicated, the current base is adopted when none was recorded or validated for equality, subject to bus range width when firmware tables are ignored. Otherwise discovery is attempted and on success the control is programmed for a single full segment; failure disables further probing.
A configuration base is acceptable when its required window ends at or below 0xFD00000000 or when the base starts at or above 0x10000000000.

Base discovery runs once on the boot processor with early PCI access and a recognized bridge identifier. It derives the top of memory from system configuration, aligns a candidate above it, collects high memory windows, orders them, and selects a placement below the lowest, above the highest, or in a sufficiently large gap, accepting only placements satisfying the validity predicate.

A boot option controls visibility of a hardware random capability through a static flag initially cleared. Missing or unrecognized values leave the flag cleared, with unrecognized values rejected as invalid, while the word force sets the flag.

Hiding is inactive without suspend support, when the capability is already absent, or when forced visible. Otherwise a configuration bit is cleared and the change is verified; success withdraws the capability with a one time notice mentioning the override, while unchanged state indicates virtualized ignoring of the control and yields a distinct one time notice.

LN setup unconditionally sets a decode configuration bit for an erratum. JG setup only invokes the random capability hiding check. BD setup first disables a cache way filter on models 0x02 to 0x1f through fault tolerant access when relevant bits are clear, then invokes the same hiding check.

Match tables built by a helper macro associate vendor family model with a stepping interval and a required microcode minimum held in a generic data field, terminated by an empty entry; evaluation compares that minimum against the boot processor revision.
A dedicated table records minimum microcode levels for family 0x17 model 0x01 stepping 2 and model 0x31 stepping 0 affected by a numbered erratum, terminated by an empty entry for later checks.

Extended leaf 0x8000001f reports encryption support and address reduction, leaf 0x80000005 reports cache associativity for alignment, leaf 0x0f with subleaf 1 reports monitoring parameters, and leaf 0x01 reports random number support.

Multiprocessor use on early models outside defined model and stepping thresholds with multiprocessor capability triggers a one time warning and marks the kernel as running on out of specification hardware with unreliable dependency tracking; qualifying combinations return silently.
Unrecognized family model combinations during generation classification emit a one time warning identifying the family and model and leave generation indicators unset.
When a lightweight wait capability is present, delay handling switches to that mechanism. When faulting on user CPUID access is reported, a fault enforcement capability is forced.
